title: Davis Museum reunites century-old Antioch mosaics and artifacts from four U.S. museums
summary: A new exhibition at the Davis Museum at Wellesley College brings into focus the ancient Greco-Roman city of Antioch. Opening on September 25, 2026, this free exhibition invites everyone to view objects reunited from American museums while examining how a 1930s archaeological excavation shaped what museum curators and historians know — and do not know — about the past. Excavating Antioch: The Archaeology of an Ancient City explores Antioch-on-the-Orontes, now Antakya, Türkiye, across two periods: the ancient city from its founding in 300 B.C.E. through the 12th century, and the 1930s excavation that shaped the formation of museum collections in the United States and Europe. title: Christie's presents Herbert Lust: Collector, Scholar, Friend
summary: Christie's announced The Collection of Herbert Lust will be a headliner of New York's Fall Marquee Week of Sales. The collection comes from the home of the ingenious collector, author, and banker Herbert Lust, who was beloved by artists, luminaries and fellow collectors for his generosity, wit and endless curiosity. Mr. Lust was a scholar with a voracious appetite for seeking out knowledge and philosophical truth. He acquired art with a studied deliberation, filling his home with thought-provoking examples of modern, post-war and contemporary works he was drawn to both aesthetically and intellectually—many of which were made by artists with whom he shared deep personal bonds, notably Alberto Giacometti and Robert Indiana. The fruitful, lifelong relationships he came to share with cultural icons of the twentieth century had a seismic impact on Mr. Lust's life, shaping both the arc of his brilliant art collection as well as the throughlines of his core identity. title: Important previously unknown work by Bellotto to be offered for sale
summary: An important, previously unknown work, The Karlskirche Vienna, by the great view painter Bernardo Bellotto is to be offered for sale at Dorotheum on 21 October 2026. Bernardo Bellotto painted the famous topographical views of Vienna that shape our image of the city as it was at the height of Habsburg power. An important, newly discovered view of the Karlskirche, Vienna painted by the celebrated vedutist will be offered in Dorotheum’s Old Masters auction on 21 October 2026. The imposing Karlskirche, built to mark the end of the last great scourge of the plague, was designed by Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach and completed in 1739. It is thought this view of the church was painted during, or shortly after, Bellotto’s stay in Vienna between 1759 and 1761. The work has recently been confirmed as a fully autograph work by Bernardo Bellotto, who was the nephew and pupil of the celebrated Venetian view painter, Canaletto. title: Gagosian explores René Magritte's enduring influence in landmark London exhibition
summary: Gagosian presents an exhibition dedicated to René Magritte and his enduring influence on the art of today, opening on September 24 at the Grosvenor Hill gallery in London. Organized in collaboration with the Fondation Magritte, This Is Still Not a Pipe: The Afterlife of Magritte examines the artist’s legacy through significant paintings, works on paper, and sculpture from all periods of his career. Featuring loans from museums and private collectors, these include some of his best-known subjects, from apples and pipes to bowler hats and cotton-cloud skies. They are juxtaposed with works by more than forty artists of different generations, many of which have been created specifically for the exhibition, in a striking installation inspired by the iconic and paradoxical aspects of Magritte’s practice. title: Nicole M. Crawford named Executive Director of Barry Art Museum
summary: Nicole M. Crawford, an experienced museum leader, curator and scholar known for connecting art with teaching across academic disciplines, has been named executive director of Old Dominion University’s Barry Art Museum. Crawford began her new role on September 21 after serving as director and chief curator of the University of Wyoming Art Museum. Her appointment comes at a defining moment for the Barry Art Museum as construction continues on a $23 million expansion that will double its gallery space and create new opportunities for exhibitions, education and community engagement. “I wasn’t actively looking to leave Wyoming, so it would have taken a very special opportunity to make me consider a move,” Crawford said. “The Barry Art Museum was that opportunity. title: Chinese works of art aales total $26M at Christie's
summary: After two days, two sales, and 234 lots that ranged across millennia, medium, style, and technique, Christie's Chinese Works of Art auctions showed a vibrant market asserting its strength. Together, Ritual, Cosmos, and Imperial Splendor: Important Chinese Art from a Private North American Collection and Important Chinese Art Including Ceramics from the Art Institute of Chicago totaled $25,966,160, more than two times the combined low estimate. The sale series began with Ritual, Cosmos, and Imperial Splendor: Important Chinese Art from a North American Private Collection, which totaled $8,695,680, or 1.7 times its low estimate, and was 94 percent sold by lot. The Important Chinese Art Including Ceramics from the Art Institute of Chicago auction made $17,270,480, realizing 2.5 times the sale's low estimate. title: Sotheby's Hong Kong high jewelry sale reaches HK$268 million as rubies lead the market
summary: Rubies, historic signed jewels and increasingly sought-after colored gemstones drove Sotheby’s latest High Jewelry auction in Hong Kong to HK$267.5 million (US$34.1 million), marking the fifth consecutive season of growth for the house’s high jewelry sales in the city. The auction drew bidders from 32 countries, with an average of 5.2 bidders competing for each lot. Nearly half of all bidders — 46 percent — were age 40 or younger, a figure Sotheby’s pointed to as evidence of a changing collector base increasingly interested in distinctive design, provenance and unusual gemstones. At the center of the sale was a rare Mauboussin Art Deco ruby and diamond necklace dating to the 1930s. The elaborate jewel sold for HK$16 million (US$2.04 million), comfortably surpassing its HK$11 million high estimate. title: Rachel Feinstein explores classical myth and feminine archetypes in Athens show
summary: Gagosian presents Rachel Feinstein’s debut exhibition in Greece. Opening on September 24, Fates features new sculptures, mirror paintings, and works on paper that engage with classical Greek motifs to address archetypes of femininity, memory and memorials, and the intersection of mythology with everyday life. The exhibition’s centerpiece is a pair of large caryatid sculptures (both 2026) that combine the female figure with architectural forms. These works explore the caryatid’s Hellenic roots, as well as subsequent Roman, Renaissance, and Neoclassical interpretations; Auguste Rodin’s sculpture Fallen Caryatid Carrying Her Stone (1881–82); and Agnes Varda’s short film Les dites cariatides (1984). title: CHAUSSEE 36 Photography unveils 'Enchanting Colour' spanning 1940s masters to post-digital light
summary: CHAUSSEE 36 Photography presents the group exhibition "ENCHANTING COLOUR", exploring the creative possibilities of colour photography from the 1940s to the present day. Conceived around an unprecedented dialogue between seven major figures in the medium and the contemporary work of Berlin-based artist Marta Djourina, the exhibition examines the enchanting -almost magical- properties of colour and its capacity to transcend reality. On this occasion, a selection of iconic works from the Collection De Gambs, including prints never before shown to the public, will be unveiled across various genres: fashion, nude, and experimental photography. title: Japanese painter Daichi Takagi explores non-duality and 'Suchness' at David Zwirner
summary: David Zwirner announces Suchness, an exhibition of new paintings by Japanese artist Daichi Takagi, on view in The Upper Room at the gallery’s London location. This is the first solo presentation of Takagi’s work in the United Kingdom. Blurring the boundary between figuration and abstraction, Takagi’s recent work is introspective and reflective, focusing on phenomena observable in his everyday environment. Motifs such as trees, stones, rain, and the moon recur across compositions, alluding to the natural world but more powerfully to the fleeting nature of perception. As Takagi describes, his practice begins with seeing and perceiving objects as pure experience. In his work, the distinction between subject and object, inside and outside, is not fully resolved, and the world emerges as a raw and immediate presence. title: National Air and Space Museum's Bezos Learning Center construction begins
summary: The Smithsonian’s National Air and Space Museum has begun construction on the Bezos Learning Center building located at the east end of the museum on the National Mall in Washington, D.C. Site preparation work started earlier in 2026, and contractor Clark/Smoot/Consigli moved into the next phase of work this month. The three-story structure will contain two floors of education and programming spaces as well as offices for the center’s team. These include flexible project, presentation and studio spaces to allow for a wide range of programs that inspire learners to pursue science, technology, engineering, arts and math (STEAM) innovation. title: PSA Mint 9 Pikachu Illustrator card sells for $5 million in record $12.1 million TCG auction
summary: A PSA Mint 9 Pikachu Illustrator boasting a Mike Baker Authenticated Gold Diamond enhancement to its grade sold for $5 million — the highest amount ever paid for a PSA 9 Illustrator and the second highest amount paid at auction for any Pokémon card — at Heritage Auctions’ Sept. 18–19 Trading Card Games Signature® Auction. The result led the two-day auction to a total of $12,182,188, smashing Heritage’s previous Trading Card Games auction record of $7,790,094 set at the June 26–27 Trading Card Games and Manga Signature® Auction by more than $4 million. It continued the five-auction streak of besting the total sales record set by the previous auction by Heritage Auctions, the world’s leading Trading Card Games auctioneer. The copy is one of 15 certified by PSA with a Mint 9, with only one example graded higher. It is the only 9-graded copy to earn the MBA Gold Diamond, indicating it is exceptional for its grade. title: William S. George Collection takes center stage in Heritage's Oct. 6-9 GACC U.S. Currency Auction
summary: A named collection of fractional currency, specimens, experimentals and courtesy autographs so robust that it fills an entire session will be among the top attractions at Heritage’s GACC U.S. Currency Signature® Auction Oct. 6–9. “Heritage’s GACC auction is an exceptional event, as impressive in quality as it is in the scope of its nearly 2,300 lots,” says Raiden Honaker, Heritage’s Director of U.S. Currency. “The lots in this auction include unquestioned highlights in virtually every category of paper money, from Fractionals to Confederate notes to National Bank Notes, in a trove that has appealing options for a wide range of collectors.” The William S. George Collection includes 479 lots, including one of just two known uncut pairs of a Fr. 1373a 50¢ Milton 3r50.9 Third Issue Justice Uncut Pair PMG Choice About Unc 58 EPQ. title: Sotheby's Hong Kong watch auction brings HK$426 million and sets new Cartier record
summary: Sotheby’s Hong Kong recorded HK$426 million (US$55 million) in its latest Important Watches auction, the highest total for a watch sale in the auction house’s history and, according to Sotheby’s, the most valuable watch auction ever staged in Asia. The two-day sale drew more than 2,000 bidders from 50 countries, reflecting the increasingly international market for rare and historically significant watches. One of the most closely watched lots was a unique white gold Cartier Cheich wristwatch dating to around 2010. Following competitive bidding from collectors in the room, online and by telephone, the watch sold for HK$26.52 million (US$3.41 million), setting a new auction record for a Cartier wristwatch. title: MS68 1792 Half Disme headlines Heritage's rarity-filled GACC U.S. Coins Auction
summary: The world’s finest example of one of the most significant coins in the history of American numismatics will grab the spotlight when it crosses the auction block at Heritage’s Oct. 8–9 GACC U.S. Coins Signature® Auction. The 1792 H10C Half Disme, Judd-7, Pollock-7, R.4, MS68 PCGS, from the Ronald Firman Collection, is modest in physical size, but commands massive numismatic significance. “This is a remarkable trophy for the most serious of collectors, the only example of this remarkable coin to earn the MS68 grade from PCGS,” says Todd Imhof, Executive Vice President at Heritage Auctions. “Its exceptional grade is only magnified by its numismatic significance, as the first federal U.S. coins struck for circulation under the authority of the Mint Act of April 2, 1792. title: Rare signed Michael Jordan baseball card leads Heritage Auctions fall sports sale
summary: Michael Jordan’s unexpected turn on the baseball diamond produced the biggest result in Heritage Auctions’ Sept. 18-19 Fall Sports Card Catalog Auction, as a signed card celebrating that remarkable chapter in his career sold for $625,250 to lead the event to $19,758,916. The 1995 Upper Deck SP Top Prospects Michael Jordan (Autograph) PSA EX-MT 6, PSA/DNA Auto 10 - MBA Gold stood atop an auction that demonstrated demand across the sports card market, from premium modern issues featuring Jordan and Shohei Ohtani to exceptional graded sets from some of the most important years in Topps history. Jordan’s brief pursuit of professional baseball with the Chicago White Sox organization in 1994-95 remains one of the most fascinating detours in modern sports history. title: Largest survey to date of the work of Arthur Jafa opens at the New Museum
summary: The New Museum presents the largest museum survey exhibition to date of the work of Arthur Jafa (b. 1960, Tupelo, MS) on view September 24, 2026, through January 3, 2027, spanning two floors of the newly expanded New Museum to encompass the full breadth of the artist’s practice. Alongside the premiere of new work, Arthur Jafa: I Am Tony will feature Jafa’s most celebrated films, including Love is the Message, The Message is Death (2016) and the Golden Lion-winning The White Album (2019), as well as recent paintings, large-scale video and film installations, and a range of sculptural and photographic objects. Over a nearly forty-year career, Arthur Jafa has sought to find new visual forms to capture the rhythm and realities of Black life in America. title: Sayre Gomez returns to Xavier Hufkens with solo exhibition 'Sim City'
summary: Sim City, Sayre Gomez’s third exhibition at Xavier Hufkens, brings together a new body of paintings, figurative sculptures, and works on paper that continue his engagement with the urban framework of Los Angeles and the mechanisms of image making. Employing various strategies of constructing and manipulating images, Sim City wrestles with representations of a city that is itself a symbol of artifice, presenting Los Angeles emerging as a cultural construction—a protagonist and backdrop, home and fantasy, paradise and myth. At the core of Gomez’s practice lies a sustained interest in examining the foundations and history of how images are made, reproduced, dissected, reanimated and how they function in contemporary culture. title: National Gallery reveals artists for summer blockbuster Full Throttle
summary: The National Gallery of Australia announces the featured artists in Full Throttle, an exhibition exploring the art and culture of one of the most potent and persistent symbols of the modern era: the automobile. Bringing together over 200 works by over 60 artists and collectives, Full Throttle will open at the National Gallery in Kamberri/Canberra on 5 December 2026, showing until 11 April 2027. Fuelled by the legacy of the film Mad Max, Full Throttle presents the car as a lens through which to examine contemporary life. Featuring works in a range of medium including sculpture, painting, installation, textiles, video and works on paper, Full Throttle showcases leading First Nations, Australian and international artists who have examined the myths, meanings and cultural power of the car. title: Dimitris Neveskiotis debuts surreal ceramic canvases in solo show at Kalfayan Galleries
summary: Kalfayan Galleries presents the first solo exhibition of Dimitris Neveskiotis, titled “We were never really here”. The opening of the exhibition will take place on Thursday 24 September 2026, from 19:00 to 21.00. The text accompanying the exhibition is written by Christos Parides. A few thoughts about Dimitris Neveskiotis: The trajectory may seem expected, but it is by no means a given: painter, sculptor, ceramicist. In this order, from his studies to the present day, these three identities point to the steps that Dimitris Neveskiotis has taken, ultimately arriving at the place from which he essentially began: painting. Even if it may appear that he is devoted to ceramics. For although the practice with which he feels most at home is indeed pottery, in the end everything leads back to painting. title: Sotheby's inaugural Nightcap festival brings $14.3 million in wine and spirits sales
summary: Rare Burgundy, historic Champagne and one of the world’s most coveted bottles of Japanese whisky helped Sotheby’s inaugural Nightcap wine and spirits festival generate $14.3 million across five auctions in New York. The week-long program, staged at Sotheby’s Breuer headquarters, combined auctions with tastings, dinners and other events, bringing together collectors, producers and enthusiasts from more than 27 countries. The final total surpassed the combined presale estimate of $8.8 million to $12.6 million. Nightcap achieved a 97 percent sell-through rate, with 62 percent of lots selling above their high estimates. The festival’s most valuable individual lot was Karuizawa 1960 Cask #5627, known as “The Prototype,” which sold for $625,000 against an estimate of $400,000 to $600,000. title: French artist Michel Verjux explores perception and architectural light at A arte Invernizzi
summary: On Thursday, 24 September 2026, at 6 p.m., A arte Invernizzi opens a new solo exhibition by Michel Verjux, a French artist with whom it has a long-standing relationship, which began in 2001 with their first collaboration. Since 1983, Verjux has been developing his artistic practice through éclairages – light installations consisting of projections of geometric figures – squares, cones, cylinders and other shapes – conceived in close relation to the architecture and the specific characteristics of the location in which they are created. By treating light as the primary element of his artistic language, the artist explores the act of seeing as a point of encounter with reality, whilst leaving room for action, thought and feeling: his investigation into the limits of perception takes place by generating a continuous dialogue between space, vision and presence, transforming each

title: 50 years of Modern Art by 100 British artists at Southampton City Art Gallery
summary: This autumn, Southampton City Art Gallery will stage an extensive exhibition of over 100 works showcasing how British artists responded to the Modern Art revolution that swept across Europe and beyond. It has been over a century since Roger Fry caused an art sensation in Britain with his 1910 exhibition Manet and the Post-Impressionists. 23 years later Herbert Read’s seminal book Art Now reviewed how the mostly France-based avant garde artists had impacted the British art scene. Art Then!
